limitations: The requested ApoMarioHighscore type, recordRunEnd(ApoMarioLevel), highscore panel, and store format do not exist in the inspected repository, so their exact new symbols and line anchors cannot be cited; proposed enforcement points are anchored to existing callers/integration methods.
The code model and outline were used for existing symbol identities and sink tags; no existing highscore-specific entry point or persistence API was present.
The inspected level parser is binary and shared-server capable, but its complete downstream allocation behavior and all caller paths were not exhaustively traced.

nodes.label: Highscore records: player name, score, survival time, ordering, and persistence
Highscore storage file and its availability across runs
Local highscore file into parser, in-memory records, and menu display
nodes.sink: ApoMarioHighscore's record parser/storeRun state and the dedicated highscore menu panel's rendered name/score/time rows.
nodes.source: The store file passed to ApoMarioHighscore(Path); the current repository has local-file persistence patterns in ApoMarioConstants#loadProperties().
nodes.untrusted_input: Bytes and text in the Path supplied to ApoMarioHighscore, which the desktop user can edit or replace.

nodes.label: Finished run state into highscore record
nodes.source: ApoMarioLevel#getPlayers(), ApoMarioPlayer#getPoints(), ApoMarioPlayer#getTeamName(), and ApoMarioLevel#getTime() at the completion path.
nodes.untrusted_input: Locally tamperable in-game player points, player name/team name, visibility/death state, and level countdown at completion.

nodes.label: Local or shared-server level bytes into level allocation and completion inputs
nodes.sink: ApoMarioLevelIO#readLevel(DataInputStream), ApoMarioLevel#makeEmptyLevel(...), entity allocation, and later ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis(boolean) score/time calculations.
nodes.source: ApoIO#readLevel(boolean,String) opens either FileInputStream or URL input and delegates bytes to ApoMarioLevelIO#readLevel(DataInputStream).
nodes.untrusted_input: Binary level dimensions, time, tile values, enemy counts, coordinates, and finish coordinates from a user-selected file or URL.

nodes.label: Player points are mutable state reset by ApoMarioPlayer#init and exposed through getPoints/setPoints; player/team names are mutable strings exposed through getTeamName/setTeamName.
nodes.task_relevance: These are candidate sources for the score and name that recordRunEnd must capture.
nodes.verification: Inspect a completed one-player run and assert the captured score/name equal the selected human player's final getters before restart.

nodes.label: Level time is initialized as levelStartTime and decremented by thinkTime(delta); getTime returns the remaining countdown, while getPassedTime derives elapsed time from randomLevel time minus remaining time.
nodes.task_relevance: The feature needs a stable elapsed survival-time value and must distinguish remaining countdown from elapsed time.
nodes.verification: Complete runs at known deltas and check stored survival time is nonnegative elapsed duration formatted as mm:ss, not the remaining countdown.

nodes.label: Completion scoring occurs in ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis(boolean): it sets the win state, updates player points for win/loss branches, then switches the panel to analysis or editor.
nodes.task_relevance: This is the integration point where the highscore must observe final score before later navigation or restart changes state.
nodes.verification: Exercise both win and loss paths and verify exactly one highscore insertion occurs after score adjustments and before any restart/menu transition.

nodes.label: The panel creates menu, analysis, and game models during init, sets the menu, and loads properties; menu rendering currently draws player-selection statistics and buttons, while setMenu selects and initializes the menu model.
nodes.task_relevance: The dedicated highscore panel/view can follow the existing model lifecycle and menu navigation patterns.
nodes.verification: Open the menu through keyboard/mouse navigation and confirm the highscore view is reachable, renders all three fields, and does not alter the stored lists.

nodes.label: Existing local property persistence writes a Properties file and silently catches write IOException; loading catches IOException and prints a message before continuing with defaults.
nodes.task_relevance: Highscore persistence must define explicit rejection/reporting and must not silently discard a valid run or malformed store data.
nodes.verification: Force read/write failures in a test store and assert the new highscore API reports the rejection while preserving prior valid records.

nodes.failure_behavior: A proposed decoder control must reject invalid dimensions, counts, coordinates, time, and tile/enemy encodings and report the rejection; the file/URL caller must substitute a bounded safe level before invoking the decoder so the gameplay/highscore effect continues.
nodes.label: The existing level decoder reads width, height, time, tile values, enemy count, coordinates, and finish coordinates from DataInputStream and immediately allocates/iterates using those values without visible bounds checks; malformed local or shared-server level bytes can therefore affect allocation, loops, and the later score/time inputs.
nodes.task_relevance: The highscore's actual score and survival time are derived from a level whose content is untrusted under the fixed desktop threat model.
nodes.verification: Feed crafted local and URL-backed level streams with zero/negative/huge dimensions, counts, coordinates, and unknown tile values; assert rejection is reported and a bounded fallback level can still be played and recorded.

nodes.failure_behavior: The highscore parser rejects malformed records and reports the rejection; the panel falls back to an empty valid board or previously loaded valid records, so menu initialization still completes.
nodes.label: A user-edited highscore file could inject malformed names, negative or overflowing scores/times, duplicate/misaligned fields, or oversized input; reachable consequences include corrupted descending order, memory/resource exhaustion, or misleading displayed results.
nodes.task_relevance: The new Path-based store and persistence API crosses a local-file trust boundary before records are displayed and reused.
nodes.verification: Use property-based and boundary tests for malformed UTF/text, negative/extreme integers, truncated records, duplicate fields, and oversized files; assert rejection is reported and the board remains bounded and sorted.

nodes.failure_behavior: At this completion integration point, select the intended human player, normalize missing/invalid name and elapsed time to explicit safe defaults, and invoke recordRunEnd once after final score calculation; the storeRun operation rejects invalid arguments and reports the rejection, while the caller's normalized values preserve the highscore insertion effect.
nodes.label: If recordRunEnd trusts locally tampered mutable player state or records after the score-changing completion logic, a user can forge a player's name/points/time or create duplicate/inaccurate entries; this violates the authenticity and integrity of the highscore.
nodes.task_relevance: The task explicitly requires the running game to record the real finished run values on both clearing and losing.
nodes.verification: Run win/loss tests with one human, AI opponent, null name, extreme mutable values, repeated setAnalysis calls, restart, and replay; assert one normalized record per eligible run and exact final score/time.

nodes.failure_behavior: The panel renders only validated, length-bounded records with index-aligned fields; invalid display data is replaced with a stated safe display value at the caller before rendering, while parser/store rejection is reported.
nodes.label: A highscore display that interpolates untrusted names or misaligns parallel name/score/time lists could expose arbitrary text, crash rendering, or show a score under the wrong player; the current menu renders user-derived player/team strings directly.
nodes.task_relevance: The dedicated panel is a new sink for persisted names and scores.
nodes.verification: Render names containing control characters, long Unicode text, missing values, and mismatched list lengths; assert clipping/safe fallback and index alignment without exceptions.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject and report malformed file records or invalid storeRun arguments; at the panel integration point, use an empty valid board/default normalized run input so the menu/highscore effect still occurs.
nodes.label: ApoMarioHighscore's Path-store parser and storeRun operation shall accept only structurally complete, bounded records with valid score, survival-time, and name fields, maintain equal-length aligned lists, sort records by score descending, and reject/report invalid input without substitution inside the operation.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects persisted highscore integrity and availability while implementing the required public API.
nodes.verification: Unit-test constructor loading and each public getter/storeRun path with malformed, boundary, duplicate, and valid records; assert rejection reporting, aligned lists, descending scores, and bounded allocation.

nodes.failure_behavior: The caller normalizes missing/invalid name and elapsed-time values to explicit defaults before calling the store; the store rejects invalid arguments and reports the rejection, and the normalized caller path still records the run.
nodes.label: The completion integration shall record one eligible finished run after ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis has applied the final win/loss score changes, using the intended human player's actual final score and name plus elapsed survival time formatted as mm:ss; replay/AI eligibility and duplicate completion behavior shall be explicitly handled.
nodes.task_relevance: Satisfies the core requirement to record clearing and losing runs from the running game itself.
nodes.verification: Integration-test both win and loss completions, one-player and AI-opponent configurations, null/blank names, repeated completion callbacks, restart, and replay; compare persisted tuple to final in-memory values.

nodes.failure_behavior: At the display caller, use a safe display fallback for a missing/invalid value and skip no valid row; the underlying parser/store rejects invalid persisted records and reports them.
nodes.label: The dedicated highscore menu panel shall display index-aligned persisted player name, score, and mm:ss survival-time rows, and navigation from the existing menu shall not mutate records.
nodes.task_relevance: Satisfies the required menu display while preserving the integrity of stored data.
nodes.verification: Automate menu navigation/rendering with zero, one, maximum, and malformed persisted rows; assert every valid row displays aligned name/score/time and stored getter lists remain unchanged.

nodes.failure_behavior: The file operation rejects/reports I/O or format failures; the panel substitutes an empty valid board for unreadable data and continues initialization, while a successfully accepted in-memory run remains available for the current menu view.
nodes.label: The highscore persistence operation shall persist accepted runs across process runs using the supplied Path, with a bounded, deterministic format and an explicit reported failure result/exception; it shall not silently discard an accepted run.
nodes.task_relevance: Satisfies persistence across runs and makes storage failures observable.
nodes.verification: Write accepted records, construct a fresh ApoMarioHighscore on the same Path, compare all getters and ordering, then inject unreadable/permission/partial-file failures and assert explicit reporting plus current-run availability.

nodes.failure_behavior: Parser/store rejects and reports; the panel uses the stated empty-board fallback and continues initialization.
nodes.label: At the highscore parser/store enforcement point, validate record count, record framing, UTF/name length, integer ranges, nonnegative bounded score and survival time, and list alignment before allocation or insertion; reject and report invalid input. At ApoMarioPanel initialization, replace an unreadable store with an empty valid board so the feature remains usable.
nodes.task_relevance: Operational control for R1 against crafted local highscore files and oversized inputs.
nodes.verification: Fuzz and boundary-test the parser/store with truncated, oversized, negative, overflowing, duplicate, and invalid-encoding records.

nodes.failure_behavior: Caller fallback preserves one record insertion with normalized values; storeRun rejects and reports any value that remains invalid.
nodes.label: At ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis(boolean), compute the eligible human player and final tuple once after all branch-specific point awards, normalize null/blank/overlong names and invalid elapsed time to explicit safe defaults before storeRun, and guard the completion transition so repeated callbacks cannot insert duplicates. storeRun still rejects invalid arguments and reports rejection.
nodes.task_relevance: Operational control for R2 and resistance to local score/name/time tampering at the primary effect integration point.
nodes.verification: Test win/loss, human/AI, null names, extreme values, repeated setAnalysis, restart, and replay; assert one accepted normalized tuple per eligible run.

nodes.failure_behavior: Use the caller's stated safe display fallback for invalid/missing values while continuing to render valid rows; parser/store rejection remains reported.
nodes.label: At the display integration point, iterate only over the validated common record length, render names with a bounded safe representation, and obtain score/time by the same index; do not permit display code to mutate the highscore lists.
nodes.task_relevance: Operational control for R3 against malformed persisted display data and row misalignment.
nodes.verification: Render hostile and boundary names plus mismatched/empty lists and assert no exception, no cross-row field mixing, and no mutation.

nodes.failure_behavior: Persistence rejects/reports the failed operation; initialization falls back to an empty valid board without suppressing gameplay or menu effects.
nodes.label: At persistAcrossRuns, serialize a bounded complete snapshot using a temporary file and atomic replacement where supported; report all I/O, encoding, and replacement failures. On load, reject partial/corrupt snapshots and initialize an empty valid board at the panel caller so the current game/menu remains available.
nodes.task_relevance: Operational control for R4 and the persistence asset's availability/integrity.
nodes.verification: Round-trip across fresh instances and fault-inject temporary-file, replacement, encoding, and partial-snapshot failures.

nodes.label: Run unit, property-based, and integration tests for ApoMarioHighscore's constructor, storeRun, getters, and persistAcrossRuns, plus menu navigation/rendering and completion hooks.
nodes.task_relevance: Verifies R1-R4 and controls C1-C4 across parser, allocation, storage, completion, and display sinks.
nodes.verification: Pass criteria: malformed input is reported and bounded, accepted records remain aligned and descending, final win/loss tuples are recorded once, display is safe, and a fresh instance reads the persisted board.

nodes.label: Inspection did not establish whether highscore records should include replay sessions, AI-controlled players, editor-created levels, or only normal one-human runs; the existing code has separate replay/editor paths and a player AI field, but no highscore policy.
nodes.task_relevance: This choice changes which completion flows are eligible and whether locally replayed or AI-generated values reach the highscore sink.
nodes.verification: Define and test the eligibility policy for normal, replay, AI, and editor flows before final integration.

nodes.label: Inspection did not establish the intended highscore file location, format, maximum number of records, or whether the supplied Path may point outside the working directory; these choices affect path handling, allocation bounds, and persistence failure behavior.
nodes.task_relevance: The public constructor accepts a Path store, but no repository code defines the new store contract.
nodes.verification: Specify the path policy and limits, then test absolute/relative paths, missing parent directories, symlinks, and oversized record counts.

summary: Inspection found no existing highscore type or persistence path. The game already exposes mutable player points/name and level time, finalizes scoring in ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis, routes panel state through ApoMarioPanel#setMenu, and reads user/server-controlled level bytes through ApoIO/ApoMarioLevelIO. The proposed feature therefore adds local-file parsing/storage and a menu view at those integration points.
